cohort: The study included 36 confirmed cases of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) identified from a population-based congenital anomaly register in the West Midlands region between 1995 and 2012.
finding: Prenatal ultrasound demonstrated relative sensitivity and specificity in diagnosing sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT), with good survival rates observed in live-born cases despite high perinatal and infant mortality for certain risk factors like solid vascular tumour composition, polyhydramnios, prematurity, and rapidly growing tumours.
followup_time: Up to 1 year post-birth for infant mortality
